title: H3039 (124th General Assembly): SC Constitutional Carry Act of 2021

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2020-12-09; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess124_2021-2022/prever/3039_20201209.htm (LegiScan doc 2220012))
provenance.note: Introduced 2020-12-09 (large file; read in full). Struck: references to a concealed weapons permit in Sections 16-23-20, 16-23-420, 16-23-430, 16-23-460, 16-23-465, 51-3-145, 23-31-220, 23-31-225 and 23-31-240; the permit-holder ID duties and $25 fine in 23-31-215(K); the 'reciprocal state' training and background-check test and the Georgia/North Carolina limit in (N); and the five-year permit revocation in (M) and 23-31-225. Unchanged: school and college carry limits apply to all persons, and the list of banned places in (M). Section 1 is the short title 'South Carolina Constitutional Carry Act of 2021'. Section 13 (23-31-240) is cut to remove the permit condition. Passage vote: none listed; introduced text only.

operative_text:
Section 2 (Section 10-11-320(B)): This section does not apply to a person who possesses a firearm and is authorized to park on the capitol grounds or in the parking garage below the capitol grounds.
Section 3 (Section 16-23-20(A)(17)): a person who is not prohibited from possessing firearms under state law, whether or not the person is a resident of the State.
Section 3 (Section 16-23-20(B)): Unless a person first obtains authorization to possess a handgun from a person with the apparent authority to grant it, nothing in subsection (A)(17) authorizes carrying of a handgun into any location prohibited under Section 23-31-215(M).
Section 6 (Section 16-23-460(C)): The provisions of this section also do not apply to handguns, rifles, shotguns, dirks, slingshots, metal knuckles, knives, or razors unless they are used with the intent to commit a crime or in furtherance of a crime.
Section 10 (Section 23-31-215(N)(1)): Valid out-of-state permits to carry concealable weapons held by a resident of another state must be honored by this State.
Section 10 (Section 23-31-215(N)(2)): Notwithstanding the reciprocity requirements of item (1), South Carolina shall automatically recognize concealed weapon permits issued by any other state.
Section 10 (Section 23-31-215(O)): (3) carrying a concealable weapon in a manner not prohibited by law.
Section 12 (Section 23-31-225): No person may carry a concealable weapon into the residence or dwelling place of another person without the express permission of the owner or person in legal control or possession, as appropriate.
